subject: Data purge vs masking: scenario guidance for MedSolutions regulated records

Subject: Data purge vs masking: options for patient PII/PHI retention windows

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re mapping our retention commitments for a new medtech pilot and need clarity on two scenarios before we finalize procurement:

1) Short-term retention with aggressive redaction: customer records retained for 30 days, then redacted to remove direct identifiers (names, SSNs, patient IDs) but keep clinical notes for analytics.
2) Minimal retention + reversible pseudonymization: retain full records for 1 year but pseudonymize identifiers so we can re-link for clinical follow-up if the patient consents.

Questions: which of these are feasible on Redwood Private (VPC) with your KMS/HSM options? What are recommended deletion semantics and audit evidence we can provide for SOC2/ISO audits? Also attaching our inventory and a short policy summary.

Appreciate a concise pros/cons memo and any suggested language we can include in the SOW.

—Priya
Dr. Priya Sharma

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear scenarios and the inventory — that’s super helpful. Quick high-level: both approaches are supported, but they have different operational trade-offs and evidence profiles. I pulled our engineering and compliance leads into the thread to give specific implementation and audit guidance.

High level pros/cons (short):
- 30-day redaction: lowest long-term storage cost; simpler from a compliance viewpoint if you can accept irreversible redaction of certain fields. Provides a clear audit trail for deletion events, but you lose the ability to re-associate records.
- 1-year pseudonymization: preserves re-linkability for follow-up but requires stronger key management and stricter access controls + HSM-backed KMS; higher storage/cost and longer audit window.

Action items I suggest: 1) Marissa to outline technical redaction/pseudonymization flows for Private deployment; 2) Priyom to confirm recommended audit artifacts and SOW language; 3) I’ll draft SOW bullets for both options and include suggested acceptance criteria.

I’ll slot a 30-minute call if helpful — are you available Thursday morning?

Priya / Kimberly —

Following up with details on how we typically implement each approach on Redwood Private (VPC):

Scenario A — 30-day irreversible redaction
- Ingestion: PII/PHI ingested to isolated tenant; initial write retained in encrypted blob storage for 30 days.
- Redaction job: scheduled Lambda-like worker triggers TTL deletion on primary fields and applies irreversible hashing on name/SSN fields. Clinical notes can be retained but run through a field-level scrubbing pipeline to remove direct identifiers.
- Audit evidence: deletion event logs, object lifecycle transition logs, and redaction job run logs (signed, timestamped). We can export a manifest of object IDs deleted for audit.
- Limitations: irreversible — no re-linking. Analytics on de-identified notes is supported but labeled as anonymized.

Scenario B — 1-year reversible pseudonymization
- Ingestion: data encrypted at rest, identifiers tokenized via HSM-backed KMS; tokens stored separately with strict access ACL.
- Re-linking: re-identification requires KMS authorization and a custodial re-link process with RBAC + dual-approval.
- Audit evidence: key access logs (HSM/KMS), tokenization events, re-identification approval records, and retention audit manifests.
- Limitations: increased KMS operations and storage; requires legal acceptance of tokenization as sufficient de-identification for your jurisdiction.

SOW wording suggestions (short):
- For redaction: "Redwood will perform irreversible redaction of specified direct identifiers after X days and provide deletion manifests and signed job logs as evidence."
- For pseudonymization: "Redwood will tokenize identifiers using customer-managed KMS with HSM protection; re-identification will require documented dual-approval and will be recorded in re-identification logs."

I attached a sketch of the data flow and an example manifest format (see links). Happy to run through the flow on a call.

—Marissa

Priya / team —

From a compliance and evidence perspective (SOC2 / ISO / HIPAA considerations):

- Evidence set for 30-day redaction: signed deletion manifests, storage lifecycle logs, irreversible-hash algorithm description (deterministic vs salted), and a rationale that de-identified notes meet your regulatory definition for analytics. Confirm whether regulators in your jurisdiction accept hashing as irreversible; we recommend truncation + one-way hashing with per-tenant salt to reduce re-identification risk.

- Evidence set for 1-year pseudonymization: KMS key rotation policy, HSM access logs, tokenization event logs, role-based access authorizations, and documented re-identification approval workflow. The re-identification workflow must be retained in your records.

A few legal prompts you should confirm with Legal Ops:
1) Are patient consents obtained for re-linking? If not, pseudonymization may not be permissible.
2) Does your legal counsel accept tokenization as de-identification for the intended analytics use?
3) Any regional residency rules that force deletion sooner than your policy (e.g., certain EU member state rules).

Suggested minimum SOW acceptance criteria (we can put verbatim):
- Deletion: Redwood will provide a signed manifest within 24 hours of scheduled retention jobs containing object IDs, timestamps, and job signature.
- Tokenization: All tokens generated using customer-managed KMS; re-identification requests will require dual-approval and be logged with requestor, approver, timestamp, and purpose.

If you want, I can draft the SOW bullets into a short addendum you can attach to your procurement paperwork.

—Priyom Das
Security & Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
